verses.sanskrit: युधिष्ठिर उवाच। इदं मे तत्त्वतो राजन् वक्तुमर्हसि भारत । अहिंसयित्वाऽपि कथं ब्रह्महत्या विधीयते ॥१॥
verses.english: Yudhishthira said O descendant of Bharata's race, you should answer this question of mine truly and in detail. What are those circumstances under which a person may become guilty of Brahmanicide without actually killing a Brahmana.

verses.sanskrit: भीष्म उवाच। व्यासमामन्त्र्य राजेन्द्र पुरा यत्पृष्टवानहम् । तत्तेऽहं संप्रवक्ष्यामि तदिहैकमनाः शृणु ॥२॥
verses.english: Bhishma said Formerly, O king, I had one day requested Vyasa to explain to me this very subject. I shall now describe to you what Vyasa told me on that occasion. Do you listen to it with rapt attention.

verses.sanskrit: चतुर्थस्त्वं वसिष्ठस्य तत्त्वमाख्याहि मे मुने । अहिंसयित्वा केनेह ब्रह्महत्या विधीयते ॥३॥
verses.english: Going to Vyasa, I addressed him saying You, O great ascetic, are the fourth in descent from Vaishishtha! Do you explain to me this. What are those circumstances under which one becomes guilty of Brahmanicide without actually killing a Brahmana?

verses.sanskrit: इति पृष्टो मया राजन् पराशरशरीरजः । अब्रवीन्निपुणो धर्मे निःसंशयमनुत्तमम् ॥४॥
verses.english: Thus addressed by me, the own begotten son of Parashara, o king an adept in the science of morality gave me the following answer at once excellent and fraught with certainly.

verses.sanskrit: ब्राह्मणं स्वयमाहूय भिक्षार्थे कृशवृत्तिनम् । ब्रूयान्नास्तीति यः पश्चात्तं विद्याद्ब्रह्मघातिनम् ॥५॥
verses.english: You should know that man as guilty of Brahmanicide who having of his own accord invited a Brahmana of pious conduct to his house for giving him alms then refuses too give anything on the pretence of there being nothing in the house.

verses.sanskrit: मध्यस्थस्येह विप्रस्य योऽनूचानस्य भारत । वृत्तिं हरति दुर्बुद्धिस्तं विद्याद्ब्रह्मघातिनम् ॥६॥
verses.english: You should, O Bharata, know that man as guilty of Brahmanicide who destroys the means of living of a Brahmana well-read in the Vedas, and all their branches and who is shorn of attachments to worldly creatures and goods.

verses.sanskrit: गोकुलस्य तृषार्तस्य जलार्थे वसुधाधिप । उत्पादयति यो विघ्नं तं विद्याद्ब्रह्मघातिनम् ॥७॥
verses.english: You should o king, know that man to be guilty of Brahmanicide who puts impediments in the way of thirsty kine while engaged in satisfying that thirst.

verses.sanskrit: यः प्रवृत्तां श्रुतिं सम्यक् शास्त्रं वा मुनिभिः कृतं । दूषयत्यनभिज्ञाय तं विद्याद्ब्रह्मघातिनम् ॥८॥
verses.english: You should take that man as guilty of Brahmanicide who, without studying them, finds fault with the Shrutis that have come down: from preceptor to pupil for ages and ages together, or with those scriptures that have been composed by the Rishis.

verses.sanskrit: आत्मजां रूपसंपन्नां महतीं सदृशे वरे । न प्रयच्छति यः कन्यां तं विद्याद्ब्रह्मघातिनम् ॥९॥
verses.english: You should know that man as guilty of Brahmanicide who does not confer upon a suitable bridegroom his daughter endued with beauty and other excellent qualities.

verses.sanskrit: अधर्मनिरतो मूढो मिथ्या यो वै द्विजातिषु । दद्यान्मर्मातिगं शोकं तं विद्याद्ब्रह्मघातिनम् ॥१०॥
verses.english: You should know that foolish and sinful wightought to be guilty of Brahmanicide who pains the Brahmanas to the very core of their hearts.

verses.sanskrit: चक्षुषा विप्रहीणस्य पंगुलस्य जडस्य वा । हरेत यो वै सर्वस्वं तं विद्याद्ब्रह्मघातिनम् ॥११॥
verses.english: You should know that man to be guilty of Brahmanicide who robs the blind, the lame, and idiots.

verses.sanskrit: आश्रमे वा वने वाऽपि ग्रामे वा यदि वा पुरे । अग्निं समुत्सृजेन्मोहात्तं विद्याद्ब्रह्मघातिनम् ॥१२॥
verses.english: You should know that man to be guilty of Brahmanicide who sets fire to the hermitage of ascetics or to forests or to a village or a town.
